newsitem.title: USA: ADM declines comment on USDA ruling.
newsitem.headline: ADM declines comment on USDA ruling.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co (ADM) declined to comment Friday on a U.S. Department of Agriculture decision to allow it to continue to do business with the government despite its guilty plea to price-fixing charges.
"We have no comment whatsoever," ADM spokeswoman Karla Miller said.
ADM pleaded guilty in October to two counts of fixing the prices of lysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, a food additive, and agreed to pay a record $100 million in fines.

As a condition to continue doing business with federal programs, ADM signed an agreement giving USDA access to company records to ensure managers are warned against violating antitrust laws and setting company policies to follow the law.
USDA on Friday also said it suspended three former ADM officials from government contracts pending the outcome of indictments. They are Michael D. Andreas, Terrance Wilson and Mark Whitacre.
